explanation:
The function $f(x) = \frac{1}{5}(x-13)^2 + 7$ is in vertex form $f(x) = a(x-h)^2 + k$ where $a = \frac{1}{5} > 0$, $h = 13$, and $k = 7$. Since $a > 0$, the parabola opens upward and has a minimum value at the vertex. The minimum value is $k = 7$, occurring when $x = 13$.

Why C is incorrect:

This is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex ($h = 13$), not the minimum value of the function. The minimum value occurs at $x = 13$ but equals $f(13) = 7$.
